parts.title: Trebuchet?!
parts.summary: For each line of a multi-line calibration document, locate the earliest and latest ASCII decimal digits, combine them into a two-digit number (repeating a sole digit), and return the sum across all lines.
parts.algorithmSummary: Converging two-pointer scan parameterized by a DigitExtractor strategy: scan inward from index 0 and from line.length - 1 via AsciiDigitExtractor, yielding O(L) worst-case / sublinear average time and O(1) auxiliary space per line with zero-churn extensibility for Part 2.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Parameterizing calibrateLine with a DigitExtractor strategy lets Part 2 plug in spelled-word matching with zero changes to 2023/day01/shared/.
Storing DigitMatch spans (value, start, length) cleanly supports both single-character ASCII digits and overlapping multi-character word matches.

parts.title: Trebuchet?!
parts.summary: Extend calibration extraction so valid digits include both ASCII 0–9 and lowercase spelled English words one through nine (excluding zero), resolving overlapping word pairs like twone and oneight before summing all per-line calibration values.
parts.algorithmSummary: First-character bucketed SpelledDigitExtractor plugging into 2023/day01/shared with zero churn: checks ASCII digits first then dispatches at most two startsWith comparisons per starting letter during converging two-pointer scans, differentially verified across all 8 overlapping word pairs.
parts.complexity: O(L) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Because 'one'..'nine' are prefix- and substring-free, scanning right-to-left down to first.start + 1 handles all 8 overlapping word pairs (twone, oneight, etc.) without backtracking or consuming regex traps.
Partitioning overlapping highlight spans into [first.start, last.start), [last.start, first.end), and [first.end, last.end) keeps rendered text verbatim in the visualizer.

parts.title: Cube Conundrum
parts.summary: Determine which cube-drawing games are possible with a bag containing 12 red, 13 green, and 14 blue cubes (drawn with replacement) and return the sum of the possible game IDs.
parts.algorithmSummary: Per-game peak envelope filter over immutable CubeBag and GameRecord value objects in 2023/day02/shared/: compute each game's component-wise minimumBag dynamically and check fitsWithin(12, 13, 14), differentially verified against a standalone early-exit reveal scanner over 500 synthetic games.
parts.complexity: O(T) time, O(G + R) space
learnings: Computing GameRecord.minimumBag as a component-wise CubeBag join handles Part 1 feasibility (fitsWithin) and Part 2 bag power (minimumBag.power) with zero parser or model churn.
Delegating non-negative safe-integer and id>=1 validation exclusively to CubeBag and GameRecord avoids unreachable duplicate branches in the parser.

parts.title: Cube Conundrum
parts.summary: For each cube-drawing game, find the minimum possible bag counts of red, green, and blue cubes across all reveals, compute each bag's power (red * green * blue), and sum all powers.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2023/day02/shared GameRecord.minimumBag and CubeBag.power with safe-integer overflow guards in O(R) time and O(1) auxiliary space per game, differentially verified against a standalone raw-text streaming scanner over 500 synthetic games.
parts.complexity: O(R) time, O(1) auxiliary space per game
learnings: Reusing GameRecord.minimumBag and CubeBag.power directly delivered Part 2 with zero edits to 2023/day02/shared/ and zero imports from part1/.
Guarding both individual bag power and cumulative sum with Number.isSafeInteger catches adversarial synthetic overflows cleanly while keeping CubeBag.power ergonomics.

parts.title: Gear Ratios
parts.summary: Parse a 2D engine schematic of unsigned multi-digit numbers, empty dots, and symbols, and sum all distinct part numbers that have at least one digit 8-way adjacent to any symbol.
parts.algorithmSummary: Symbol-centered 8-neighbor lookup over an encapsulated Int32Array cell-to-part-ID grid inside EngineSchematic (reusing shared/core Grid2D and DIRS_8), deduplicating touched PartNumber spans by ID via a Uint8Array bitset; differentially verified against a perimeter-box scan oracle up to 140x140.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Hyphens ('-') appear immediately adjacent to digits in personal inputs; always scan unsigned [0-9]+ spans and treat '-' strictly as a schematic symbol.
Encapsulating a flat Int32Array cell-to-part-ID spatial index inside EngineSchematic.adjacentNumbersOf(symbol) unifies Part 1 union-of-parts and Part 2 degree-2 '*' gear ratios with zero churn.

parts.title: Gear Ratios
parts.summary: Identify every '*' gear symbol 8-way adjacent to exactly two distinct part numbers on the engine schematic, compute each gear ratio (a * b), and return the sum of all gear ratios.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2023/day03/shared EngineSchematic.adjacentNumbersOf(symbol) and SchematicSymbol.isGearCandidate with exact BigInt ratio products (a * b) in O(R * C) time; differentially verified against a standalone number-border-scatter oracle up to 140x140.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Unlike Part 1, a single part number shared between two gears (e.g. 10*20*30) contributes to both ratios, so Part 2 must never apply a global visited-part bitset when summing ratios.
Deriving GearTraceFrame.isGear from adjacentParts.length === 2 rather than ratio > 0n preserves zero-valued gears like 0*5 while keeping BigInt products overflow-safe.

parts.title: Scratchcards
parts.summary: For each scratchcard listing winning numbers and your numbers, count how many of your numbers match a winning number, score 2^(k - 1) points for k > 0 (or 0 for k = 0), and sum the points across all cards.
parts.algorithmSummary: Hash-set winning-number lookup on immutable Scratchcard value objects in 2023/day04/shared/: derive matchingNumbers, matchCount, and doubling points dynamically with safe-integer overflow guards in O(N * (W + H)) time; differentially verified against both a BigInt bitset oracle (reusing shared/core bitCount) and a sorted two-pointer oracle over 250 synthetic cards.
parts.complexity: O(N * (W + H)) time, O(W) auxiliary space per card
learnings: Keeping Scratchcard.matchCount dynamic in 2023/day04/shared/ lets Part 2 copy-cascade DP reuse the exact parsed cards and match counts with zero churn.
Guarding both per-card points (k <= 53) and cumulative sums with Number.isSafeInteger prevents silent IEEE-754 precision loss on large synthetic match counts.

parts.title: Scratchcards
parts.summary: Under the cascading copy rule where each scratchcard instance with k matches wins one copy of each of the next k cards below it (with won copies triggering identical downstream cascades), compute the total number of original and copied scratchcards.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn O(N) forward difference-array DP in exact BigInt reusing 2023/day04/shared Scratchcard.matchCount: maintains an O(1)-update delta wave across cards with table-end clamping; differentially verified against both an O(N * K) forward scatter oracle and an O(N) backward suffix-sum dual oracle up to 2^65.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Allocating delta with length N + 1 and gating on end > i collapses zero-match firebreaks and last-card clamping into one clean branch with zero out-of-bounds guards.
Using BigInt for copy counts plus shared/core bigintLog2 and BigInt ratio scaling keeps both 2^65 synthetic cascades and the Log2/Linear SVG wave visualizer overflow-free.

parts.title: If You Give A Seed A Fertilizer
parts.summary: Translate a list of initial seed IDs sequentially through seven category-conversion maps of piecewise range shifts (mapping uncovered values to identity) and return the lowest resulting location ID.
parts.algorithmSummary: Sorted RangeMap binary-search pipeline in exact BigInt built on shared/core ClosedInterval in 2023/day05/shared/ (O(sum R_m log R_m + S * sum log R_m) time): validates non-overlapping source intervals and contiguous category chains while keeping raw seeds and sorted rules zero-churn for Part 2 interval splitting; differentially verified against a raw file-order linear-scan oracle across 25 random multi-stage almanacs.
parts.complexity: O(sum R_m log R_m + S * sum log R_m) time, O(R) space
learnings: Storing raw BigInt seeds and sorted disjoint RangeRule intervals in 2023/day05/shared/ supports Part 1 binary-search lookups while leaving Part 2's 1.84-billion-seed interval splitting zero-churn.

Almanac rule lines order destination before source (destStart srcStart length) and reach 2^32, so explicit BigInt sorting (< / > / 0) and ClosedInterval inclusive ends (start + len - 1n) prevent silent overflow and off-by-one bugs.

parts.title: If You Give A Seed A Fertilizer
parts.summary: Reinterpret the seeds header as (start, length) pairs of inclusive seed ranges (~1.845 billion seeds on personal input), propagate all seed ranges through the seven category-conversion maps, and return the minimum resulting location ID.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn forward two-pointer interval splitting and IntervalUnion coalescing in exact BigInt reusing shared/core ClosedInterval/IntervalUnion and 2023/day05/shared Almanac/RangeMap in O(S * (P + R) log(P + R)) time; differentially verified against both an exhaustive per-seed brute-force oracle on 25 small-range almanacs and a backward critical-endpoint pullback oracle on 20 huge-scale (> 2^32 and > 2^53) almanacs.
parts.complexity: O(S * (P + R) log(P + R)) time, O(P + R) space
learnings: In a two-pointer sweep across sorted intervals and sorted range rules, advance ruleIdx only when matchEnd === rule.source.end so a second disjoint interval falling inside the same wide rule still matches it.
Coalescing mapped output ribbons through shared/core IntervalUnion after each stage keeps interval count linear in rule count even across 1.845 billion seeds and non-injective overlapping outputs.

parts.title: Wait For It
parts.summary: Given a table of toy-boat race durations T and record distances D where holding for h ms travels h * (T - h) mm, count how many integer hold times strictly beat the record in each race and return their product.
parts.algorithmSummary: Exact BigInt shifted-discriminant quadratic formula (Delta' = T^2 - 4(D + 1)) with monotone Newton-Raphson bigintIsqrt and shared/core ClosedInterval in 2023/day06/shared/ (O(N log log T) time, branch-free tie exclusion), plus reusable RaceParabolaVisualizer in 2023/day06/shared/viz/; exhaustively verified against a direct-hold-scan oracle (0 <= T <= 40) and a monotone binary-search oracle up to T = 10^18.
parts.complexity: O(N log log T) time, O(N) space
learnings: Using the shifted integer discriminant Delta' = T^2 - 4(D + 1) with exact BigInt floor square root makes Delta' >= 0 both necessary and sufficient for >= 1 winner and automatically excludes ties without floating-point rounding bugs.
Flagging 2023/day06/shared/math.ts (bigintIsqrt) for end-of-year promotion into shared/core/math.ts keeps shared/ read-only during parallel solves while preparing zero-churn Part 2 reuse.

parts.title: Wait For It
parts.summary: Ignore kerning spaces on the Time and Distance rows to merge all digits into a single long boat race, and count how many integer hold durations strictly beat the merged record distance.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2023/day06/shared BoatRace, RaceSheet, bigintIsqrt, and RaceParabolaVisualizer with a 9-line kerning-stripped parser: solves h(T - h) >= D + 1 in exact BigInt Newton steps in O(log log T) time; differentially verified against an independent monotone binary-search oracle across ties, peak boundaries, personal scale, and T > 10^20.
parts.complexity: O(L + log log T) time, O(L) space
learnings: Factoring extractRaceRows and parseUnsignedBigInt into 2023/day06/shared/parser.ts let Part 2 strip internal whitespace and reuse BoatRace, traceRaceSheet, and RaceParabolaVisualizer with zero shared-module edits.
Solving the shifted integer quadratic in exact BigInt keeps 16+ digit discriminants completely free of IEEE-754 rounding errors.

parts.title: Camel Cards
parts.summary: Rank 5-card Camel Cards hands from weakest (rank 1) to strongest (rank N) by 7 hand types and positional left-to-right card strength (2 < ... < A), then sum rank * bid across all hands.
parts.algorithmSummary: Packed 24-bit SMI strength-key sort parameterized by a polymorphic CamelHandRule in 2023/day07/shared/ with exact BigInt winnings in O(N log N) time (3.11 ms on 1,000 hands), paired with a reusable CamelCardsVisualizer in 2023/day07/shared/viz/ for zero-churn Part 2 Joker reuse; differentially verified against an independent lexicographic-comparator-sort oracle across boundary cases and 50 seeded random deals.
parts.complexity: O(N log N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Packing (handType << 20) | (s0 << 16) | ... | s4 into a 23-bit non-negative SMI gives single-subtraction comparisons and decodable hex strength keys while remaining identical across Part 1 and Part 2.
Parameterizing CamelHandRule and placing CamelCardsVisualizer in 2023/day07/shared/viz/ (outside the pure-TS shared/index.ts barrel) lets Part 2 inject Joker rules with zero shared-module churn.

parts.title: Camel Cards
parts.summary: Re-rank the Camel Cards hands treating J as a wildcard Joker that maximizes hand type while acting as the weakest literal card (J < 2 < ... < A) in positional tie-breaks, then sum rank * bid.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn greedy max-bucket CamelHandRule (jokerHandRule) plugging into 2023/day07/shared/ and CamelCardsVisualizer with zero shared edits: adds all j jokers to the largest non-joker frequency bucket (mapping all-J JJJJJ to FiveOfAKind with key 0x600000) and packs 24-bit SMI strength keys in O(N log N) time (3.51 ms on 1,000 hands); differentially verified against an independent exhaustive wildcard substitution oracle across all 19 (j, partition) patterns, 50 uniform deals, and 20 joker-heavy deals.
parts.complexity: O(N log N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Adding all j jokers to the highest non-joker multiplicity bucket (with JJJJJ -> FiveOfAKind) provably maximizes Camel Cards hand tier across all 19 (j, partition) states because the 7 hand types follow exact lexicographic partition order.

Zero-churn parameterization of CamelHandRule and CardSpotlight wildLabel highlighting delivered Part 2 in 73 lines of production domain code and a 7-line visualizer wrapper with zero edits to 2023/day07/shared/.

parts.title: Haunted Wasteland
parts.summary: Follow a cyclic Left/Right instruction tape across a directed network of labeled nodes starting at AAA and count the minimum steps needed to arrive at ZZZ.
parts.algorithmSummary: Dense Int32Array/Uint8Array finite-state walk in 2023/day08/shared/ (WastelandNetwork) with O(1) transitions, Uint8Array(N * L) visited-(node, ip) cycle detection, and alphanumeric [A-Za-z0-9]+ labels for zero-churn Part 2 reuse (1.71 ms on 750 nodes / 269-turn tape), paired with a dual-scale WastelandVisualizer (FullNetworkSvg / LocalDecisionHubSvg); differentially verified against an independent Map-based string oracle across 50 seeded random graphs.
parts.complexity: O(S) time (bounded by O(N * L)), O(N * L) space
learnings: Accepting [A-Za-z0-9]+ node labels in 2023/day08/shared/parser.ts and exposing O(1) stepFrom/labels primitives prepares Part 2's alphanumeric multi-ghost walks (11A/22Z) with zero parser churn.
Never call Object.freeze() on TypedArray instances (V8 throws TypeError); encapsulate Int32Array/Uint8Array buffers inside private fields and freeze only the owning WastelandNetwork instance.

parts.title: Haunted Wasteland
parts.summary: Simultaneously start a ghost on every node ending in 'A', advance all ghosts in lockstep along the cyclic L/R instruction tape, and return the earliest step at which every ghost simultaneously lands on a node ending in 'Z'.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn generalized rho-cycle decomposition and BigInt CRT convergence engine reusing 2023/day08/shared WastelandNetwork and shared/core ceilDiv/bigintLog2: extracts exact (prefixLength, cycleLength, preCycleHits, cycleHits) per ghost via Int32Array(N * L), checks pre-cycle simultaneous hits via the max-prefix anchor theorem, and folds multi-hit congruences via iterative extGcdBigInt (9.83 ms on 6 ghosts converging at 13.13 trillion steps); differentially verified against an independent lockstep ghost simulator across 40 seeded random multi-ghost networks.
parts.complexity: O(G * N * L) cycle extraction + O(prod |H_g| * log M) CRT time, O(N * L) space
learnings: Even the official Part 2 example contains two '**Z' hits inside a single (nodeId, ip) cycle (22A has period 6 with hits at steps 3 and 6), so generalized BigInt CRT over multi-hit cycles handles both the official example, arbitrary non-aligned prefixes/offsets, and AoC's aligned-LCM personal input cleanly.

Every pre-cycle simultaneous hit t < max(prefix_g) must appear in the max-prefix anchor ghost's preCycleHits, letting us test mixed pre-cycle and already-in-cycle convergence in O(|preCycleHits| * G) before requiring non-empty cycleHits.

parts.title: Mirage Maintenance
parts.summary: For each signed integer history in the OASIS report, build successive adjacent-difference layers until reaching an all-zero baseline, extrapolate the next rightmost value bottom-up, and sum all predicted values.
parts.algorithmSummary: Exact BigInt finite-difference DifferencePyramid with a narrow polymorphic ExtrapolationStrategy (FORWARD_EXTRAPOLATION_STRATEGY) in 2023/day09/shared/ in O(H * L^2) time (2.45 ms on 200x21 signed histories), paired with an edge-windowed DifferencePyramidViz SVG animator for zero-churn Part 2 backward extrapolation reuse; differentially verified against both an O(L) exact BigInt Lagrange/binomial convolution oracle and a recursive finite-difference oracle across 100 seeded polynomials up to degree 18 and ±10^18.
parts.complexity: O(H * L^2) time, O(L^2) per-history space
learnings: Factoring the shared bottom-up fold into DifferencePyramid.extrapolate(strategy) with a narrow ExtrapolationStrategy (anchorOf, combine) prepares Part 2 backward extrapolation in ~10 lines with zero edits to 2023/day09/shared/.

Always check row.every(v => v === 0n) (never sum === 0n or some) and fail fast on length-1 non-zero rows before stepping to empty [], avoiding silent false convergence on signed/zero-crossing sequences.

parts.title: Mirage Maintenance
parts.summary: Using the same finite-difference pyramids from the OASIS report, extrapolate one step backward to the left edge of each history (newLeft = first - belowLeft) from the all-zero baseline and sum all reconstructed preceding values.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn BACKWARD_EXTRAPOLATION_STRATEGY plugging into 2023/day09/shared DifferencePyramid, OasisReport, traceOasisReport, and DifferencePyramidViz with zero shared edits in O(H * L^2) time (2.37 ms on 200x21 signed histories); differentially verified against both an O(L) exact BigInt backward Lagrange/binomial convolution oracle and a reversed-sequence forward difference reduction oracle across 100 seeded polynomials up to degree 18 and ±10^18.
parts.complexity: O(H * L^2) time, O(L^2) per-history space
learnings: Injecting a 10-line BACKWARD_EXTRAPOLATION_STRATEGY (anchor = layer[0], combine = anchor - below) into 2023/day09/shared delivered Part 2 with zero edits to shared/ and zero imports from part1/.
Cross-checking against both closed-form backward binomial convolution and reversed-sequence forward reduction catches sign/order bugs like below - anchor immediately.

parts.title: Pipe Maze
parts.summary: Infer the hidden pipe shape at start tile S on a 2D pipe grid, trace the unique closed main loop of mutually connected pipes ignoring disconnected clutter, and find the farthest step distance from S along the loop.
parts.algorithmSummary: Deterministic 4-bit DIRS_4-aligned bitwise cycle walk in 2023/day10/shared/ (PipeMaze + immutable MainLoop storing ordered tiles and a private Int32Array cycle-index map) in O(R * C) time (6.32 ms on 140x140): derives farthestDistance = length / 2 dynamically and pairs with a dual-mode SVG/HiDPI Canvas PipeMazeCanvas with clutter toggle and Part 2 enclosed/scanline overlay props built in upfront; differentially verified against both a full-grid Wavefront BFS distance oracle and a shared/core DisjointSet component-size oracle.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Because every non-S pipe tile has degree <= 2 and S has exact degree 2 in the mutual-connection graph, walking from S can only hit a dead end or return cleanly via S's second port—eliminating unreachable visited/port branches while keeping MainLoop constructor invariants strictly enforced.

Storing the ordered loop cycle and inferred PipeShape for S in 2023/day10/shared/ plus optional enclosedMask/activeScanRow props in PipeMazeCanvas prepares Part 2 (Pick's/Shoelace + scanline parity) with zero shared-module churn.

parts.title: Pipe Maze
parts.summary: Count all non-loop tiles (both ground '.' and disconnected junk pipes) strictly enclosed inside the main pipe loop, treating parallel adjacent pipes as zero-width squeeze corridors connected to the exterior.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn row-by-row North-port (DIR_N) scanline crossing parity reusing 2023/day10/shared PipeMaze, MainLoop, and PipeMazeCanvas (enclosedMask, revealedUpToRow, activeScanRow) in O(R * C) time (9.01 ms on 140x140): stores only a private Uint8Array mask and crossingsByRow in immutable EnclosedAnalysis with dynamic count/row totals; differentially verified against both an O(L) Shoelace + Pick's Theorem oracle and a 2x-expanded squeeze flood-fill BFS verifying cell-by-cell mask equality across all 4 official examples, all 6 S shapes, and 25 seeded non-convex cluttered mazes.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Sweeping row-by-row and toggling inside on main-loop tiles whose effective mask has DIR_N (|, L, J, including resolved S) simultaneously solves squeezing corridors, counts enclosed junk pipes, and produces the exact enclosedMask for zero-churn PipeMazeCanvas playback.

Cross-checking scanline parity against both Shoelace + Pick's Theorem (scalar) and 2x-expanded BFS flood fill (cell-by-cell mask) independently validates every inferred S shape and tight corridor squeeze.

parts.title: Cosmic Expansion
parts.summary: On a 2D sky-survey grid of empty space ('.') and galaxies ('#'), double the size of every row and column containing no galaxies (expansion factor 2) and compute the sum of shortest Manhattan distances between every unordered pair of distinct galaxies.
parts.algorithmSummary: Separable 1D axis edge-cut sweep in exact BigInt (O(R * C) parse + O(R + C) sweep, 2.16 ms on 140x140) parameterized by expansionFactor: bigint via createCosmicExpansionSolver(2n) in 2023/day11/shared/, avoiding O(G^2) pair enumeration completely and pairing with a HiDPI StarfieldCanvas and CosmicExpansionVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 (1,000,000x) reuse; differentially verified against an O(G^2) pairwise expanded Manhattan oracle, a literal expanded-grid DIRS_4 BFS oracle, affine linearity up to 10^12, and symmetry invariance.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) parse, O(R + C) sweep, O(R * C) space
learnings: Decomposing Manhattan distance into independent row and column edge-cut sweeps (prefix * (G - prefix) * sliceWidth) eliminates O(G^2) galaxy pair loops completely and casts factors to BigInt before multiplying so arbitrary expansion factors stay exact.
Parameterizing createCosmicExpansionSolver(expansionFactor) and CosmicExpansionVisualizer in 2023/day11/shared/ prepares Part 2 (1,000,000n) in ~15 lines with zero shared-module edits.

parts.title: Cosmic Expansion
parts.summary: Expand every galaxy-free row and column on the sky-survey grid by a replacement factor of 1,000,000 and compute the exact sum of shortest Manhattan distances across all unordered pairs of distinct galaxies.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn PART2_EXPANSION_FACTOR = 1_000_000n specialization reusing 2023/day11/shared separable 1D axis edge-cut sweep and CosmicExpansionVisualizer with zero shared edits (2.01 ms on 140x140 in exact BigInt); differentially verified against an independent raw-text O(G^2) pairwise expanded Manhattan oracle, exact affine extrapolation S(1_000_000) = S(1) + 999_999 * (S(2) - S(1)), and an independent sorted-coordinate prefix-sum oracle.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) parse, O(R + C) sweep, O(R * C) space
learnings: Separable 1D axis edge-cut sweeping in exact BigInt solves 1,000,000x cosmic expansion in 2.01 ms with zero grid materialization and delivered Part 2 in 6 lines of production domain code with zero edits to 2023/day11/shared/.

Each empty row or column has replacement width F = 1_000_000n (net delta +(F - 1n)), confirmed by official 10x (1030) and 100x (8410) checkpoints and the exact affine law S(F) = S(1) + (F - 1) * (S(2) - S(1)).

parts.title: Hot Springs
parts.summary: Given rows of damaged-spring condition records ('.', '#', '?') paired with contiguous damaged-group length lists, count the total number of valid damaged-spring arrangements consistent with every row's pattern and group runs.
parts.algorithmSummary: Rolling-row BigInt block-placement DP with prefix operational/damaged run checks parameterized by an unfold-factor strategy (unfold = 1) in 2023/day12/shared/ in O(N * K) time per row (3.82 ms across 1,000 rows): validates every contiguous '#' placement and trailing damaged mask in O(1) via precomputed Int32Array prefix sums and pairs with an interactive HotSpringsVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 (5x unfolded) reuse; differentially verified against an independent backtracking enumeration oracle across official examples, edge cases, and seeded random spring records.
parts.complexity: O(sum(N * K)) time, O(N) working space
learnings: Precomputing Int32Array prefix counts of '.' and '#' turns each contiguous damaged-block placement check into O(1) inside a rolling BigInt DP table, keeping 1,000 rows at 3.82 ms and scaling effortlessly to Part 2's 5x-unfolded records.
Parameterizing the unfold factor in 2023/day12/shared/solverFactory.ts and HotSpringsVisualizer prepares Part 2 (5x unfold) in ~15 lines with zero edits to shared/.

parts.title: Hot Springs
parts.summary: Unfold every damaged-spring record 5x (joining 5 copies of the pattern with '?' and repeating the damaged-group counts 5 times) and compute the exact sum of valid arrangements across all unfolded rows.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn PART2_UNFOLD_FACTOR = 5 specialization reusing 2023/day12/shared rolling-row BigInt suffix block-placement DP, O(1) dot-prefix checks, and HotSpringsVisualizer with zero shared edits (18.19 ms across 1,000 unfolded rows up to length 104 / 30 groups, totaling 37.36 trillion arrangements in exact BigInt); differentially verified against an independent top-down memoized (pos, groupIdx, currentRun) BigInt DP oracle, closed-form binomial C(L' - sum(G') + 1, |G'|) checks exceeding Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, cross-boundary '#' bridging, and 35 seeded PRNG unfolded records.
parts.complexity: O(sum(L' * G')) time, O(L') working space
learnings: Parameterizing unfoldFactor inside 2023/day12/shared/solverFactory.ts and HotSpringsVisualizer reduced Part 2 to 7 lines of domain code and a 14-line visualizer wrapper with zero edits to shared/ or part1/.

Rolling-row BigInt suffix DP computes 37.36 trillion unfolded arrangements across 1,000 rows in 18.19 ms on the main thread, while bigintLog2 keeps the interactive DP heatmap overflow-free even past 2^53.

parts.title: Point of Incidence
parts.summary: Locate the unique vertical or horizontal mirror reflection axis in each ash/rock pattern grid (ignoring overhanging edges) and sum columns to the left of vertical axes plus 100 times rows above horizontal axes.
parts.algorithmSummary: Arbitrary-width BigInt row/column bitmask Hamming scanner using shared/core bitCount parameterized by targetSmudges (0 for Part 1) in 2023/day13/shared/ in O(R * C + R^2 + C^2) time (2.70 ms across 100 patterns): enforces strict uniqueness across all vertical and horizontal axes, extracts exact mismatched SmudgePair coordinates via lowest-set-bit iteration, exposes ReflectionMatch.mirrorOf() for thin presentation, and pairs with MirrorGridSvg/IncidenceVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 (targetSmudges = 1) reuse; differentially verified against an independent raw-character cell scanner across official examples (0 & 1 smudges), wide 40x70 grids past bit 64, and 60+ seeded synthetic patterns.
parts.complexity: O(R * C + R^2 + C^2) time, O(R + C) space
learnings: Encoding rows and columns as arbitrary-width BigInt bitmasks with shared/core bitCount(a ^ b) eliminates 31-bit width ceilings and parameterizes both Part 1 (targetSmudges = 0) and Part 2 (targetSmudges = 1) in one shared reflection engine with zero shared-module churn.

Placing mirrorOf(row, col, pattern) directly on ReflectionMatch keeps MirrorGridSvg.tsx completely free of overhang and mirror arithmetic while supporting live mirrored-pair hover and Part 2 smudge highlights.

parts.title: Point of Incidence
parts.summary: Repair the single defective cell ('smudge') in each ash/rock pattern so that a new valid vertical or horizontal reflection line emerges (distinct from Part 1's axis), and sum the new mirror scores across all patterns.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn PART2_TARGET_SMUDGES = 1 specialization reusing 2023/day13/shared arbitrary-width BigInt row/column bitmask Hamming scanner, exact lowest-set-bit SmudgePair extraction, and IncidenceVisualizer/MirrorGridSvg with zero shared edits (2.66 ms across 100 patterns): finds the unique axis with total Hamming distance 1 and highlights both smudge coordinates automatically in the SVG viewer; differentially verified against an independent literal single-cell flip brute-force oracle (filtering out the original Part 1 axis) across official examples (400), edge/overhang/A0-destroying cases, 6x66 wide BigInt grids, and 60 seeded synthetic patterns.
parts.complexity: O(R * C + R^2 + C^2) time, O(R + C) space
learnings: Flipping a single cell changes a candidate axis's mismatch count by 0 (overhang) or ±1 (paired), so locating the unique new reflection line after fixing one smudge is mathematically identical to finding the unique axis with Hamming distance 1—delivering Part 2 in 7 lines of domain code with zero edits to 2023/day13/shared/.

Cross-checking against a literal single-cell flip brute-force oracle that excludes original Part 1 axes confirms equivalence even when the smudge lies in Part 1's overhang and keeps the old axis valid.

parts.title: Parabolic Reflector Dish
parts.summary: Tilt a 2D platform of rolling rounded rocks ('O') and immovable cube rocks ('#') north so all rounded rocks slide as far north as possible, and sum the north-beam load (height - row) of every rounded rock.
parts.algorithmSummary: Unified 4-direction flat Uint8Array line sweep via a SweepSpec dispatch table (north/west/south/east) inside immutable DishPlatform in 2023/day14/shared/ in O(H * W) time (2.60 ms on 100x100): encapsulates a private Uint8Array (never frozen) with dynamic northLoad/roundedCount/rowLoads getters and TextDecoder('ascii') fingerprint() ready for zero-churn Part 2 spin-cycle detection, paired with a HiDPI DishCanvas + per-row load bar chart; differentially verified against both an independent 4-direction bubble-step gravity simulator (40 seeded grids + spin cycles) and a zero-mutation direct arithmetic column-load accumulator (60 seeded grids).
parts.complexity: O(H * W) time, O(H * W) space
learnings: Parameterizing north, west, south, and east tilts through one SweepSpec dispatch table eliminates 4x direction boilerplate and prepares Part 2's N-W-S-E spin cycles and fingerprint() hashing with zero shared-module churn.

Using TextDecoder('ascii') on a flat ASCII-byte Uint8Array gives both O(H * W) board fingerprints and clean toLines() slicing while keeping DishPlatform frozen without ever calling Object.freeze() on the TypedArray.

parts.title: Parabolic Reflector Dish
parts.summary: Repeatedly run complete 4-direction spin cycles (North, West, South, East) on the rock platform for 1,000,000,000 cycles and return the resulting total north-beam load.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn hash-map rho-cycle detection reusing 2023/day14/shared DishPlatform.tilt(), TILT_DIRECTIONS, TextDecoder('ascii') fingerprint(), and DishCanvas with zero shared edits (51.52 ms on 100x100): keys states strictly by full board fingerprint (avoiding north-load collisions) to locate exact (cycleStart, cycleLength) and projects 1,000,000,000 via cycleStart + ((targetCycles - cycleStart) % cycleLength) in O(1), paired with a RhoLoadChart trajectory SVG preserving closure and projection milestones; differentially verified against an independent Floyd's Tortoise-and-Hare O(1)-memory cycle oracle and direct brute-force spin simulation across official examples (64), fixed points, immediate loops, and 40 seeded random dishes.
parts.complexity: O((mu + lambda) * H * W) time, O((mu + lambda) * H * W) space
learnings: Keying rho-cycle detection on full DishPlatform.fingerprint() rather than northLoad prevents false early cycle detection when distinct board states share equal north loads (as occurs in cycles 2 and 3 of the official example).

Exposing buildTraceFromAnalysis alongside optional targetCycles on traceSpinCycles both avoids double-simulating in DishPart2Visualizer and makes the acyclic (cycleStart === null) trace path 100% testable.

parts.title: Lens Library
parts.summary: Compute the ASCII HASH value (starting at 0, repeating ((h + ascii) * 17) mod 256 per character) for every comma-separated step in the initialization sequence (ignoring newlines) and return their sum.
parts.algorithmSummary: Iterative Horner bitwise HASH accumulation (((h + code) * 17) & 255) in 2023/day15/shared/ in O(C) time (1.76 ms across ~4,000 steps): exposes HashCharTransition, traceHashCharacters, parseInitSequence, and shared/viz/HashPipelineRibbon for zero-churn Part 2 HASHMAP reuse, paired with a 16x16 bucket heatmap whose HashSequenceFrame derives runningSum dynamically from bucket counts; differentially verified against an independent exact BigInt base-17 polynomial oracle across 'HASH' (52), all 11 official example steps (1320), long tokens past period 16, and 120 seeded random ASCII sequences.
parts.complexity: O(C) time, O(N) space (O(1) per-token hash)
learnings: Deriving HashSequenceFrame.runningSum dynamically as sum(b * bucketCounts[b]) guarantees the 16x16 bucket heatmap and cumulative telemetry stay in exact sync with zero stored derived state.
Placing hashAscii, traceHashCharacters, parseInitSequence, and HashPipelineRibbon in 2023/day15/shared/ prepares Part 2's 256-box HASHMAP lens procedure with zero shared-module churn.

parts.title: Lens Library
parts.summary: Execute the HASHMAP lens-installation procedure across 256 ordered boxes (removing by label on '-' or inserting/replacing in place on '=f' using HASH(label) as the box index) and return the total focusing power sum of (box + 1) * slot * focalLength.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn polymorphic LensInstruction hierarchy (RemoveLensInstruction / UpsertLensInstruction) executing against an encapsulated 256-Map OpticalBench reusing 2023/day15/shared hashAscii, parseInitSequence, traceHashCharacters, and HashPipelineRibbon with zero shared edits in O(C + sum boxLen) time (3.52 ms on ~4,000 instructions): derives focusingPower, occupiedBoxCount, totalLensCount, rawToken, and boxIndex dynamically with zero stored derived state, paired with an interactive OpticalBenchRack slot-chip visualizer; differentially verified against an independent array-of-256-arrays + BigInt base-17 polynomial hash oracle across the official example (145), box-3 collision churn, and 120 seeded random instruction sequences.
parts.complexity: O(C + sum boxLen) time, O(B + L) space
learnings: Using JavaScript Map per box preserves insertion order on in-place replacement (set on existing key) and shifts trailing entries forward on delete, while a single findLensSlot helper shared by upsert and remove eliminates unreachable fallback branches.
Reusing 2023/day15/shared hashAscii, parseInitSequence, traceHashCharacters, and HashPipelineRibbon delivered Part 2 with zero edits to shared/ and zero imports from part1/.

parts.title: The Floor Will Be Lava
parts.summary: Trace a light beam entering the top-left corner (0, 0) traveling east across a 2D optical contraption of mirrors ('/', '\') and splitters ('|', '-'), terminating cycles via directed-state tracking, and count all distinct energized tiles.
parts.algorithmSummary: Unified flat-queue Int32Array(4 * H * W) wavefront BFS kernel inside BeamTracer with a 20-byte outgoing-direction bitmask table and reusable Uint8Array(H * W) visited masks in 2023/day16/shared/ in O(H * W) time (1.42 ms on 110x110): handles entry-tile optics at (0, 0) (which is '\' in personal input), exposes 2-pass bounded-memory sampled tracing (O(maxSteps * H * W)), Contraption.edgeEntries(), and ContraptionCanvas with optional Part 2 perimeter score ring for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against an independent plain-JS Set<string> + switch oracle across the official 10x10 example (46), all 40 perimeter entries (max 51), closed mirror/splitter cycles, and 40 seeded random contraptions.
parts.complexity: O(H * W) time, O(H * W) space
learnings: Personal input places a '\' mirror directly at (0, 0) unlike the official example's '.', so energizing and evaluating entry-tile optics on Wave 0 before stepping is essential.

Unifying solve() and 2-pass bounded-memory traceWaves() on one reusable Int32Array wavefront BFS kernel eliminates code duplication while keeping all 440 Part 2 perimeter trials zero-allocation and zero-churn.

parts.title: The Floor Will Be Lava
parts.summary: Evaluate every inward perimeter entry beam (top heading south, bottom heading north, left heading east, right heading west) across the 2D optical contraption and find the maximum number of energized tiles achievable.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reusable BeamTracer full perimeter scan over all 2 * (H + W) Contraption.edgeEntries() reusing 2023/day16/shared optics, BeamTracer, and ContraptionCanvas perimeter heatmap with zero shared edits in O((H + W) * H * W) time (39.47 ms across all 440 perimeter entries on 110x110 with zero per-entry TypedArray allocations): encapsulates frozen PerimeterScanResult (deriving best dynamically with strict '>' first-entry tie-breaking and zero stored derived state) and single-tracer traceOptimalPerimeter feeding ContraptionCanvas's rim heatmap ring; differentially verified entry-for-entry against an independent plain-JS Set<string> full-perimeter oracle across official example (51 at (0, 3) S), 1x1, rectangular, corner-asymmetric, loop-heavy, and seeded random contraptions.
parts.complexity: O((H + W) * H * W) time, O(H * W) space
learnings: Storing only frozen scores inside PerimeterScanResult and computing best dynamically eliminates stored derived state, while traceOptimalPerimeter reuses one BeamTracer for both the 440-port perimeter scan and optimal wavefront capture.

Pre-building Contraption.edgeEntries(), reusable BeamTracer TypedArrays, and optional edgeScores/optimalEntry rim heatmap props on ContraptionCanvas delivered Part 2 with zero edits to 2023/day16/shared/ and zero imports from part1/.

parts.title: Clumsy Crucible
parts.summary: Route a crucible from top-left (0, 0) to bottom-right (H - 1, W - 1) on a 1..9 heat-loss grid minimizing entered block heat loss without reversing 180 degrees or moving more than 3 consecutive blocks in one direction.
parts.algorithmSummary: Axis-alternating macro-leg graph ((r, c, axis) with 2 * H * W states) + intrusive O(1) Int32Array circular DialBucketQueue in 2023/day17/shared/ parameterized by CrucibleRule(1, 3) (6.04 ms on 141x141): automatically enforces no-reversal, [minRun, maxRun] turns, and Part 2's final-leg stopping length in one unified search() pass with zero per-frame array copies in trace() and reusable HiDPI CrucibleVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 ([4, 10]) reuse; differentially verified against an independent full 4D (r, c, dir, run) 1-step binary-heap Dijkstra oracle across official examples (102 Part 1, 94 & 71 Part 2), unreachable strips, path-legality invariants, and 25 seeded rectangular grids x 4 rules.
parts.complexity: O(H * W * (M - m + 1) + D*) time, O(H * W + M) space
learnings: Contracting straight runs into macro-legs on the axis-alternating (r, c, axis) graph shrinks the state space to 2 * H * W while enforcing both turn lengths and Part 2's stopping rule automatically.

Pairing a unified search() pass with an intrusive circular DialBucketQueue (bucketCount = 9 * effectiveMaxRun + 1) solves 141x141 in 6.04 ms with zero GC churn and zero divergence between solve() and trace().

parts.title: Clumsy Crucible
parts.summary: Route an ultra crucible from (0, 0) to (H - 1, W - 1) on the 1..9 heat-loss grid requiring at least 4 and at most 10 consecutive straight blocks before every 90-degree turn and before stopping at the goal.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn ULTRA_CRUCIBLE_RULE (4..10) specialization reusing 2023/day17/shared axis-alternating macro-leg CrucibleRouter, intrusive O(1) circular DialBucketQueue (<= 91 buckets), and CrucibleVisualizer with zero shared edits (8.93 ms on 141x141): automatically enforces the minimum 4-block straight run on both intermediate turns and the final stopping leg into (H - 1, W - 1); differentially verified against an independent 4D (r, c, dir, run) 1-step binary-heap Dijkstra oracle across official examples (13x13 -> 94, 5x12 -> 71), boundary/unreachable grids (1x1, 1x5, 1x11, 2x2, 1x4, 2x6, 1x12), and 20 seeded random grids.
parts.complexity: O(H * W * 7 + D*) time, O(H * W) space
learnings: Macro-leg axis-alternation (2 * H * W states) handles Part 2's 4..10 ultra-crucible rule and final-leg stopping constraint identically to Part 1's 1..3 rule with 18 lines of production domain code and zero shared-module edits.
Explicitly testing both official Part 2 examples (13x13 -> 94 and 5x12 -> 71) plus unreachable strips (2x6, 1x12) verifies both the maxRun=10 cap and the minRun=4 stopping rule.

parts.title: Lavaduct Lagoon
parts.summary: Follow orthogonal trench dig steps (U/D/L/R with distances) around a closed 1m-wide loop, excavate the enclosed interior, and compute the total cubic meters of lava the lagoon can hold.
parts.algorithmSummary: Exact BigInt Shoelace formula + Pick's theorem (A = |sum(x_i * y_{i+1} - x_{i+1} * y_i)| / 2 + P / 2 + 1) behind a reusable DigPlanDecoder strategy in 2023/day18/shared/ (1.79 ms on 758 steps): computes exact interior+boundary lattice points in O(N) time and O(N) space with zero rasterization, paired with BigInt-scaled SVG projection (supporting Part 2's 10^7-scale coordinates) and reusable LagoonPolygonVisualizer; differentially verified against both an independent bounded flood-fill raster oracle and an exact BigInt horizontal scanline oracle across official examples (62), degenerate corridors, CW/CCW orientations, and randomized rectilinear loops.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Pick's theorem combined with the exact BigInt Shoelace area computes total lattice-cell area (interior + boundary) in O(N) time without ever rasterizing a grid, making Part 2's ~10^7 hex distances effortless.
Parameterizing the shared solver by a DigPlanDecoder strategy and scaling vertices to SVG space in BigInt lets Part 2 plug in hex-encoded instructions with zero shared-module edits.

parts.title: Lavaduct Lagoon
parts.summary: Decode the true orthogonal dig instructions from the 6-digit hexadecimal color codes (first 5 hex digits as distance, final digit 0/1/2/3 as R/D/L/U) and compute the total cubic meters of lava held by the massive closed lagoon.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn HEX_DIG_PLAN_DECODER strategy plugging into 2023/day18/shared createLagoonSolver, exact BigInt Shoelace + Pick's LagoonPolygon, BigInt-scaled SVG projection, and LagoonPolygonVisualizer with zero shared edits (1.75 ms on 670 hex steps spanning ~10^7 coordinates): preserves exact precision far beyond IEEE-754 MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (~4.75 x 10^13 personal volume); differentially verified against an independent exact BigInt horizontal scanline oracle (reusing ClosedInterval & IntervalUnion from shared/core) across official example (952408144115), 10^8-side > MAX_SAFE_INTEGER polygons, and CW/CCW concave/collinear hex loops.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Injecting HEX_DIG_PLAN_DECODER into createLagoonSolver solved 10^13-scale Part 2 in 1.75 ms with 5 lines of solver code and zero edits to 2023/day18/shared/.

Testing a chained 10^8-side hex square (10,995,095,515,965,001 > Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) plus an exact BigInt horizontal scanline oracle proves zero float64 precision loss across both geometry and SVG projection.

parts.title: Aplenty
parts.summary: Route machine parts with (x, m, a, s) ratings from workflow 'in' through ordered conditional rules until accepted ('A') or rejected ('R'), and sum x + m + a + s over all accepted parts.
parts.algorithmSummary: DAG-validated WorkflowSystem (reusing DirectedGraph.topologicalOrder and ClosedInterval from shared/core) + unified 4D RatingBox interval splitter in 2023/day19/shared/ (3.04 ms across 522 workflows and 200 parts): validates all targets before cycle detection, routes each PartRating via Workflow.matchRule in O(P * D * R) time, and pre-builds exact BigInt RatingBox.split / collectAcceptedBoxes / buildBoxSplitTrace + AxisGaugeBars + WorkflowTraceVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 ([1..4000]^4) reuse; differentially verified against a standalone recursive string-rule evaluator, an exhaustive [1..6]^4 brute-force grid count, and the official [1..4000]^4 count (167409079868000n).
parts.complexity: O(V + E + P * D * R) time, O(V + E + P) space
learnings: Validating every non-terminal workflow target before constructing DirectedGraph prevents auto-synthesizing undefined targets as sinks while letting DirectedGraph.topologicalOrder() reject any self-loop or cycle in one pass.

Representing both individual PartRatings (via RatingBox.fromPart) and 4D hypercubes (RatingBox.uniform) with ClosedInterval makes AxisGaugeBars and WorkflowTraceVisualizer 100% reusable across Part 1 and Part 2 with zero mode-specific rendering branches.

parts.title: Aplenty
parts.summary: Count every distinct (x, m, a, s) rating combination in [1, 4000]^4 that is accepted ('A') by the workflow DAG starting at 'in'.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn [1..4000]^4 hyperrectangle splitter reusing 2023/day19/shared WorkflowSystem, RatingBox.uniform(1n, 4000n), countAcceptedCombinations, buildBoxSplitTrace, and WorkflowTraceVisualizer with zero shared edits (3.61 ms across 522 workflows): supports both standard two-section AoC inputs and workflow-only inputs via extractWorkflowBlock and accumulates exact BigInt accepted volumes in O(T) hyperrectangle splits; differentially verified against an independent plain-tuple recursive DFS interval oracle, pairwise 4D box disjointness + A<->R complement conservation (sum === 4000^4), and an end-to-end [1..5]^4 brute-force 625-point grid oracle.
parts.complexity: O(T) time, O(D + T) space
learnings: Gating a synthetic [1..5]^4 test workflow with in{x>5:R,m>5:R,a>5:R,s>5:R,sub} lets an exhaustive 625-point brute-force grid oracle test the unmodified [1..4000]^4 Part 2 solver end-to-end.
Pre-building RatingBox splitting and box-split visualization inside 2023/day19/shared/ delivered Part 2 with 33 lines of domain solver code and zero shared-module edits.

parts.title: Pulse Propagation
parts.summary: Simulate 1,000 button presses sending low pulses into a network of broadcaster, flip-flop (%), conjunction (&), and sink modules in FIFO order, then multiply the total low and high pulses emitted.
parts.algorithmSummary: Polymorphic CircuitNode hierarchy (BroadcasterNode, FlipFlopNode, ConjunctionNode, SinkNode via declarative NODE_FACTORIES with zero type-tag switches) + index-pointer FIFO CircuitSimulator in 2023/day20/shared/ (5.92 ms across 1,000 presses on 58 modules): computes ConjunctionNode.highCount and simulator.product dynamically in exact BigInt, exposes topology accessors (inputsOf/outputsOf/specOf), post-receive onPulse hooks, two-pass bounded PulseTraceFrame sampling, and layered SVG PulseCircuitVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 rx-feeder LCM reuse; differentially verified against an independent plain-map FIFO simulator oracle across both official examples (32000000 and 11687500), untyped sinks, multi-input conjunctions, feedback loops, and seeded random circuits.
parts.complexity: O(P * E_avg) time, O(V + E + Q_max) space
learnings: Placing ModuleDescriptor in types.ts keeps types <- nodes <- blueprint strictly acyclic while polymorphic NODE_FACTORIES eliminate type-tag switch chains across all four module kinds.

Running a two-pass bounded trace builder (fast probe pass + selective snapshot capture) keeps visualization memory O(maxSteps) while rendering Answer directly from solver.solve keeps PulseCircuitVisualizer 100% reusable for Part 2's LCM result.
